Privacy

Your conversations go to the services you choose. Context from other apps is shared only when you connect a source and send it.

Last updated: October 18, 2026.

Accounts and conversations

SwiftChat uses your configured AI providers. Provider credentials are stored in macOS Keychain. AIChat conversation records are stored locally; requests and attachments are sent to the selected provider. That provider’s terms and privacy policy govern its processing and retention.

ChatGPT sign-in and conversations run through the ChatGPT website inside WebKit. Website cookies and sign-in state are retained locally. The website owns its history; SwiftChat projects conversation-list metadata into its native sidebar. SwiftChat is not affiliated with OpenAI.

Work with Apps

SwiftChat can read text from supported sources you explicitly connect, including Safari, Terminal, TextEdit, Notes, Xcode, Codex excerpts, and native Telegram for macOS. Permissions depend on the source: Accessibility-based sources require Accessibility access; Safari also requires Automation permission and permission for JavaScript from Apple Events. Telegram reads locally synchronized cached messages, without media files.

You can preview the source and choose its available capture scope. Sources are refreshed before sending. Captured context is sent to the selected AI service and may remain in conversation history. This can include sensitive text: review the selected source before sending.

Capture is read-only. SwiftChat does not type into or edit a connected app. If capture fails, submission stops and your draft remains available.

AIChat tools and browser

With a model that supports tools, AIChat can search, read, and write files in SwiftChat’s working directory, generate interactive content, and operate the in-app browser. Tool results, page text, and screenshots can enter the conversation’s context and are sent to the selected AI service.

For long conversations, AIChat can summarize working context for subsequent requests. The original conversation and complete tool results remain in history.

Websites opened in SwiftChat receive ordinary browser requests and may store cookies. Opening a page by itself does not send its contents to an AI service; using AIChat’s browser tools can share page text and screenshots as described above.

Updates and this website

The macOS updater checks the update feed on this website and downloads releases from GitHub. These requests disclose standard connection information, such as your IP address, to the hosting providers. Automatic update checks can be managed in the app’s settings.

This website uses no advertising or analytics scripts. GitHub Pages hosts the site and GitHub hosts downloads; their infrastructure may process ordinary access logs.

Support

GitHub issues are public. Do not include API keys, cookies, personal conversations, or source documents when reporting a problem. See Support for reporting guidance.
